[USER] The user is working on a model build.  
[USER] The user is currently working on a Revell 1/48 F-15E Strike Eagle kit.  
[PREFERENCE] The user is thinking of using a mix of Vallejo Model Air paints and enamel washes to achieve a worn look.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Weathering can make or break a model, and military aircraft are particularly great subjects for weathering.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant provided general tips for achieving a realistic worn look on a military aircraft model, including:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Study reference images.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Understand the environment.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Start with a good base coat.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Use a variety of weathering products: washes, drybrushing, chalks or pastels, enamel or acrylic paints.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Focus on high-wear areas: leading edges of wings, engine intakes, landing gear, cockpit frames, areas around panel lines and rivets.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 6. Build up gradually.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 7. Blend, blend, blend.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 8. Avoid over-weathering.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 9. Add subtle streaks and stains.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 10. Practice and experiment.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 11. Reference, reference, reference.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Additional tips specific to military aircraft include considering the age and maintenance history, distinctive weathering patterns, and weathering the underside of the model.
